source.title: PatchFormer: A Patch-Based Time Series Foundation Model with Hierarchical Masked Reconstruction and Cross-Domain Transfer Learning for Zero-Shot Multi-Horizon Forecasting
source.citation: Olaf Yunus Laitinen Imanov et al., 2026
source.authors: Olaf Yunus Laitinen Imanov; Derya Umut Kulali; Taner Yilmaz

record.tranche_reason: Tests pretraining-data scaling in a time-series foundation model, extending scaling analysis to a different data domain.
record.gate_note: The paper reports one scaling result relevant to V5: PatchFormer MSE across pretraining-data sizes. Its forecasting benchmark, ablation, transfer, and efficiency results do not measure the claim versions. The scaling result concerns time-series MSE versus pretraining data, not language-model held-out cross-entropy.
record.test_reason: Reports forecasting MSE of a time-series foundation model across pretraining-data sizes from 1B to 100B points, with a fitted scaling curve. This is a new setting (time series) with a result bearing on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors state that MSE decreases log-linearly with pretraining data up to 100B points. They say this suggests continued gains from larger corpora, 'following scaling laws similar to language models'. They do not claim a power-law fit.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates time-series forecasting MSE against pretraining-data size, rather than measuring language-model held-out cross-entropy against parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.problems: The scaling result is presented in a figure, with no uncertainty estimates or comparison of alternative fit forms stated. It concerns MSE for one time-series model and pretraining data, not language-model cross-entropy.
record.rows_left_out: Other benchmark and ablation results were left out because they do not measure any listed scaling-law claim version.

untested.parts: Power-law form specifically (no alternative fits compared); scaling with parameters or compute (Base 85M vs Large 512M are never compared on loss); other modalities; repeated data; fine-tuning and transfer scaling.
Language-model pretraining loss scaling; not tested.
Extrapolation from small to large runs; not tested.
Architecture shape at fixed parameters; not tested.
Downstream predictability from scale or loss; not tested beyond the single data-scaling curve.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'challenges' label is too strong. A log-linear fit over two decades does not show that a power law fails, and the paper presents the result as consistent with LM scaling laws. Credibility concerns: the paper says pretraining uses 87B points, yet Fig. 1 extends to 100B, and how the sub-sampled runs were made is not described. The evaluation dataset for the scaling MSE is unspecified. Numbers are round, there are no error bars, and the paper is a short preprint. Researchers should weigh this result lightly.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits to small runs predict substantially larger runs.
The effect of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Only time-series pretraining-data scaling is examined; other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer scaling are not tested.
Downstream-task performance scaling or its predictability from pretraining loss.
Dependence on fitting choices or setup, and whether curves bend away from a power law.

rows.subject: PatchFormer
rows.operation_detail: Measured forecasting MSE across pretraining-data sizes.
rows.value: MSE = 0.412 − 0.045 log10(N); R² = 0.97; 1B points: MSE = 0.412; 100B points: MSE = 0.322
rows.note: The paper reports declining MSE with more pretraining data, but gives a linear-in-log10(N) fit rather than a power-law fit. The reported endpoints and fit are shown in Figure 1.
rows.check: The values check out against the fit: 0.412 at 1B and 0.322 at 100B. Smooth decline over two decades is observed, but only a log-linear fit is reported. Over this range a log-linear fit cannot be told apart from a small-exponent power law (about b≈0.054). The evaluation dataset and horizon for the MSE are not stated, so the measure is zero-shot forecasting MSE, not held-out pretraining loss. The number of points in the figure is not stated. There is no baseline.

relationships.condition: PatchFormer time-series pretraining-data scaling, 1B–100B points, single model and unstated evaluation set (Fig. 1)
relationships.reason: MSE falls smoothly with data over two decades, but the authors fit a log-linear form, not a power law. They compare no forms and report no uncertainty. This gives at most weak, form-ambiguous evidence for V5, not a clear absence (r1).
relationships.display_finding: MSE decreased smoothly over two decades of data, but the study fitted a log-linear form without comparing alternatives or reporting uncertainty.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
